title: Samsung Launches AI Health Assistant as Tech Giants Race to Own Your Wellness Data
excerpt: The AI-powered chatbot, now in beta for US users, analyzes sleep, activity, and vitals data to deliver personalized health guidance — while a parallel deal with Lark Health targets Medicare-eligible seniors.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Samsung's AI Health Assistant is now in beta for US users, analyzing various health data.
  • A partnership with Lark Health will provide free chronic disease programs for Medicare-eligible seniors starting Q3 2026.
  • The Galaxy Watch 9 will unlock advanced health coaching features, enhancing the Health Assistant experience.
  • Samsung Health remains free, contrasting with Google's $10/month Fitbit Health Premium amid privacy concerns.

Samsung Electronics has officially entered the AI health coaching race with the launch of Health Assistant, an AI-powered chatbot integrated into its Samsung Health app. The feature, now live in beta for eligible users in the United States, marks Samsung's most ambitious attempt yet to transform its wearable ecosystem from a passive data tracker into a proactive wellness platform.

"Our new Health Assistant advances Samsung's vision for Connected Care by giving users a deeper understanding of their mind and body through daily health monitoring and increasing opportunities for early detection," said Dr. Hon Pak, Senior Vice President and Head of Samsung's Digital Health team.

What the Health Assistant Actually Does

The assistant works as a conversational chatbot within Samsung Health, drawing on data across the app's five core wellness pillars: sleep, activity, nutrition, mindfulness, and vitals. Users can ask questions about their health trends — step counts, sleep quality, stress levels — and receive personalized answers grounded in their own biometric history rather than generic advice.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=PfNQIQPNYu0

Samsung says the recommendations have been "validated by a team of physicians and certified health coaches." The system is designed to identify patterns users might miss, such as how poor sleep correlates with elevated heart rate variability or reduced activity levels. It cannot diagnose or treat medical conditions — a disclaimer Samsung has made explicit from the outset.

> **"Google's Fitbit Air with Health Premium, priced at $10 per month, offers explicit plan-building and coaching."**

Galaxy Watch 9 Unlocks the Full Vision

The Health Assistant beta arrives just ahead of Samsung's Galaxy Unpacked event in London on July 22, where the company is expected to unveil the Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2. The timing is deliberate: Samsung's most advanced health coaching features are gated to the new hardware.

Daily Cardio Load, which monitors cumulative cardiovascular strain and recommends training intensity, will require the Galaxy Watch 9. So will Fitness Index, which benchmarks heart rate, VO2 max, and step counts against peer groups across five categories. The Antioxidant Index, using the watch's BioActive sensor to measure skin carotenoids as a proxy for fruit and vegetable intake, is another Watch 9 exclusive, according to Gadget Hacks.

"Our Connected Care Everywhere initiative represents a dramatic shift in how care must move away from fragmented, episodic care and toward a ubiquitous, always-on home-based health ecosystem."

— Dr. Hon Pak, SVP and Head of Digital Health, Samsung Electronics

Existing Galaxy Watch owners get a redesigned Samsung Health layout, the Vitals dashboard — which tracks five overnight biometrics against personal baselines rather than population averages — and the new Heart Health Score. But the full coaching experience requires an upgrade.

Lark Partnership Targets Seniors on Medicare

Running parallel to the consumer-facing Health Assistant is a multi-year partnership with Lark Health, announced on July 15, that aims squarely at chronic disease prevention for US seniors. Beginning in Q3 2026, adults aged 65 and older will be able to access Lark's 12 chronic disease management programs through Samsung Health at no out-of-pocket cost.

Medicare-eligible seniors get additional benefits: live clinical intervention, cellular-connected devices like blood pressure cuffs and glucometers, and enrollment in programs covering prediabetes, diabetes, hypertension, and stress management. The most comprehensive tier, Lark Medicare ACCESS, pairs AI coaching with clinical oversight and is valued at $900 per year.

Samsung's 400-million-device hardware footprint, spanning the Galaxy Watch, Galaxy Ring, and smartphones, gives the partnership immediate scale. Lark brings clinical validation: 22 peer-reviewed studies and 10 AI patents built over a decade with $180 million in R&D investment.

A Crowded and Contentious Market

Samsung's push comes as every major tech company scrambles to own the AI health coaching space. Google's Fitbit Air with Health Premium, priced at $10 per month, offers explicit plan-building and coaching. Apple is rumored to be developing its own AI health assistant. Whoop and Oura already run AI chatbots within their ecosystems.

"Google's Fitbit Air with Health Premium, priced at $10 per month, offers explicit plan-building and coaching."

Samsung Health remains free beyond hardware costs — a meaningful differentiator. But the company's approach to data collection has drawn scrutiny. In mid-July, Samsung Health introduced a consent toggle asking users to allow their health data, including medication records, menstrual cycle tracking, and wearable biometrics, to be used for AI training. Users who declined initially received a warning that their synced data would be deleted. Samsung later clarified that opting out only removes data collected specifically for AI training, not existing health records, according to Digital Trends.

What This Means for the Indian Diaspora

Samsung's Galaxy devices have a significant footprint among Indian-Americans, and the Lark partnership addresses conditions disproportionately affecting South Asian populations. Type 2 diabetes prevalence is roughly four times higher among South Asians compared to white populations in the US, and cardiovascular disease risk runs elevated across the diaspora. Free Medicare-covered programs for prediabetes and hypertension management, accessible through a device many already own, could prove particularly relevant for older family members.

The Health Assistant beta is limited to the US for now, with no timeline announced for expansion to India or other markets. Samsung's Galaxy Unpacked event on July 22 may shed more light on global availability.
